country.comment: Empirical fieldwork conducted across 22 sub-counties in 3 rural districts of Uganda, alongside analysis of Ugandan national water and local government policies.

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative institutional analysis reporting descriptive coding frequencies of interview excerpts rather than statistical effect estimates on household or water-point outcomes.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Across 93 local government interviews (625 coded references to service delivery influences and 110 to infrastructure development influences), regulative influences such as formal policies and mandates accounted for only 15% of cited influences on service delivery support (cited by 62% of respondents) and 31% on infrastructure development support (cited by 23% of respondents), whereas normative influences (34% of service delivery references; 32% of infrastructure development references) and cultural-cognitive influences (24% and 16%, respectively) predominated. The authors conclude that Uganda's 2019 National O&M Framework alone is insufficient to motivate local government support for professionalized rural water maintenance unless aligned with normative community and political expectations, leader identities, and adequate central-to-local fiscal transfers (with 40% of actors discussing infrastructure development citing resource constraints and 14 actors citing delayed or reduced central government disbursements).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 10-17, Results & Table 3; PDF pp. 19-20, Conclusions
